## Cross-array harmonisation for longitudinal EWAS

Longitudinal epigenome-wide association studies have a practical problem that is rarely
acknowledged in the analysis: cohorts recruited over several years are often typed on
more than one array generation. Baseline samples sit on the Illumina Infinium 450K
BeadChip, follow-up samples on the EPIC array. The two platforms share only part of
their probe content, and the probes they do share do not always behave identically.

My doctoral work develops a reproducible framework for combining the two generations in
a single longitudinal analysis — probe filtering, normalisation and batch handling
chosen so that the array generation does not become the dominant source of variance, and
the whole thing packaged so that it can be rerun rather than described.

The framework is being developed on a longitudinal cohort of **126 samples from 38
individuals**, and implemented as reusable Galaxy and R components rather than a
one-off script.

::: {.callout-tip appearance="simple"}
Code: [`ewas-crossarray-harmonise`](https://github.com/kkamieniecka/ewas-crossarray-harmonise) —
reproducible cross-array harmonisation and region detection for longitudinal EWAS.
:::

## Pharmacoepigenomics of clozapine response

Clozapine is the only drug licensed for treatment-resistant schizophrenia (TRS), and
response to it varies widely between patients. The thesis asks how much of that
variation is visible in the methylome, and whether routinely generated array data can
support the kind of precision-psychiatry decisions that are currently made on clinical
grounds alone.

A concrete negative result matters here as much as the positive ones: methylation arrays
**improve sample-identity quality control** in longitudinal designs, where sample
mix-ups are a real risk, but the SNP content they carry **cannot substitute for proper
CYP genotyping** when the question is drug metabolism. Reporting that boundary honestly
is part of the contribution.

## Earlier work: cancer genomics and liquid biopsy

At the CRUK Manchester Institute I built and maintained containerised Nextflow pipelines
for cell-free DNA and DNA methylation analysis across Linux, HPC and cloud environments,
supporting data from **184 patients** across multi-centre studies, with pipeline work
contributing to research published in *Nature Cancer* and *Nature Communications*.

## Methods I work with

- Illumina Infinium methylation arrays (450K, EPIC): `.idat` import, QC, normalisation, DMP and DMR calling
- Nanopore methylation calling and variant analysis
- cfDNA / liquid biopsy analysis, MBD-seq, RNA-seq
- Statistical genetics: GWAS/EWAS, rare-variant analysis, PLINK
- Workflow engineering: Nextflow DSL2, nf-core, Galaxy, Docker, Singularity, AWS and HPC
- Machine learning applied to transcriptomic and methylomic features
